relevance_note: Single-patient case report of Tangier disease diagnosed biochemically and histologically ("A case of Tangier disease (TD) is reported from India."); no ABCA1 genotyping is reported for the patient.
method_note: Built by a Python script from my own reading of the paper; every span was checked verbatim by script. In scope: the index patient (diagnosis of Tangier disease) and his four sisters, described only as a group whose serum lipid profiles were normal; they are labelled 'sister of patient', 'sister of patient 2' to '4' and get one excluded row each (abnormal serum lipid profile, inferred from group statement). Under D-27 a normal lipid profile as a whole is not taken to exclude any specific checklist lipid item, so their checklist rows are all not reported. No ABCA1 variant or genetic testing is reported for anyone, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported (defined as patients with an ABCA1 variant) is null. 'Routine urine examination and haemograms were normal except for low platelet count' is recorded as an excluded abnormal urine examination only; it is not used to exclude reticulocytosis. Hepatomegaly is marked excluded from 'other abdominal viscera were not palpable' (clinical examination); ultrasound reported fatty liver without stating liver size. Coronary artery disease is left not reported: ECG, echocardiography and clinical cardiac evaluation were normal but the authors state coronary angiography was not done. Reduced tendon reflexes is excluded because reflexes were reported brisk in the lower limbs and normal in the upper limbs. Tonsillectomy at age seven is stated ('probably for recurrent tonsillitis', hedged), so the tonsillectomy checklist item is observed; tonsil colour is not reported because the tonsils had been removed. The Mayo clinic case (ref 4) mentioned in the Discussion is given no individual-level fact beyond 'a shorter duration of illness' and is not extracted. Table 1 (nerve conduction values, patient's right and left side) was not transcribed feature by feature; the text's summary of demyelinating neuropathy is used. No contradictions found in the paper.
